title: Starting on six-string banjo and first jobs at seventeen
summary: He began early on a banjo tuned like a guitar, subbed for John in Sam Morgan's and Celestin's bands, and was working at 17.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up a first guitar or banjo, self-taught

blocks.x: and I'll just go by that way. I just wonder if it's from the family way back in the colonial times probably. To get on with your musical education, we'll say, when you started on banjo, your brother used to help you. Oh yes. Did you play in a band pretty quick then?

Yeah, yes indeed. I played a band pretty quick. I remember my brother John sent me in his place. He was with Sam Morgan one time ago, he sent me with Sam Morgan and Kid Ora was on trombone. We was advertised in the street then, in trucks. I remember that this guy played in his place and many jobs I played in the Papa Salastain Band in my brother John's place.
Do you remember your very first job? Was that the one you substituted in Morgan's band?

No, that's not my first job, Bill. I had a lot of, when I got, I made my own band, I had a lot of jobs of my own. See, after I made up my band and got around playing little house parties and going on, I got bigger jobs. Well how old were you when you first? I was 17 years old, Bill, when I started playing.
You must have started on something before then with that musical family, didn't you?
Well Bill, I would start with my instrument. Yeah. But banjo, six string banjo.
That was tuned like a guitar then.
When you first started on your brother started helping you, were you 17 then or younger than that? Oh, younger than that Bill.
That's what I thought. Yeah, I was playing at 17. Oh yeah. Yeah, I was playing at 17. Making money, playing jobs.
That's right. Um, had you ever played any other little homemade instruments or ever blow on little flute or anything when you followed parades or?
No Bill, all my instrument was, was ghetto, banjo and drum and baseball and outside instruments I never fooled.
You never fooled making a drum set of your own
or beating on anything or anything like that? No, I never did do that Bill. Like I told you, I did try a sousa form but it was too difficult for me and I'll put it down. I'll unfold that. Yep.
